title: Drizzle with Effect
description: Query with Effect, catch a failed insert by its tag, roll back a transaction with your own error, and retry.

steps.label: A plan
steps.title: Write the query as a plan
steps.body:
This is the Drizzle query you know, written with **Effect**. `Effect.gen` and `yield*` read like `async` and `await`, but `program` is only a plan: nothing touches the database until `Effect.runPromise`.

Hover `program`. Its type says what it returns, how it can fail, and what it needs to run (`PgClient`), which `Effect.provide` hands it.

Press **Run** to see the users.

meta.summary: Select the users inside an Effect program.
meta.changed: The plan ran once `Effect.runPromise` started it, and returned Ada and Grace.

steps.label: Errors
steps.title: Catch a failed insert by its tag
steps.body:
This example deliberately inserts Ada's email twice. The unique constraint rejects the second insert.

A **tag** identifies an error type. `Effect.catchTag` handles every failure tagged `EffectDrizzleQueryError` from this insert, not just duplicate emails. Errors with other tags remain unhandled.

Here we log the query error and continue. In your application, inspect its cause before treating it as a duplicate email.

meta.summary: Insert a taken email, and handle the failure by its tag.
meta.changed: The insert failed, `catchTag` logged it, and the program went on: still two users.

steps.label: Transaction
steps.title: Roll back with your own error
steps.body:
`NotEnoughCredits` is an error of your own, tagged like Drizzle's. Inside `db.transaction`, an Effect that **fails** rolls the transaction back: no `try`, no `throw`.

Ada spends 3 credits. Grace tries to spend 50, so her update is undone and `catchTag` logs why.

meta.summary: Spend credits in a transaction that fails with your own error.
meta.changed: Ada went from `10` to `7`. Grace's update went below zero, so it was **rolled back** and she kept `5`.

steps.label: Retry
steps.title: Retry a temporary failure
steps.body:
This simulation reports a busy mail server twice, then succeeds. No email is sent. `Effect.retry({ times: 3 })` allows up to three retries after the first attempt; this simulation succeeds on attempt three.

**Retrying runs the operation again.** Only retry temporary failures when repeating the operation is safe. An insert or an email may already have succeeded even if you did not receive its acknowledgement. Keep retries around the operation you intend to repeat, not the whole program.

replace.with:
<{ readonly name: string }> {}
class MailerBusy extends Data.TaggedError("MailerBusy")<{ readonly attempt: number }> {}

meta.summary: Retry a simulated temporary failure, without repeating the database writes.
meta.changed: The simulation failed twice and succeeded on attempt three. No email was sent. Check **Logs**.
